data.ruling: The refutation stands on both points, and both are errors in the reported figure. (1) The claim says the A version has a SINAD of 71.5 dB typ. In Rev. F Table 1 that value is in the B version column only. The A version states 69 dB min over TMIN to TMAX and 70 dB min at 25 degC, and gives no typical SINAD. (2) The rms is wrong in its arithmetic: 28.945 mg / sqrt(12) = 8.356 mg, so 8.36 mg, not 8.34 mg. The core figure holds: ENOB = (69 - 1.76) / 6.02 = 11.17 bits minimum, and the step is 28.9 mg at 15 mV/V/g with a ratiometric full scale of 66.7 g. The 23-sample count also holds: ceil((8.356 / 1.75)^2) = 23. Corrected figure: 11.17 bits minimum from SINAD 69 dB min (A version, -40 to 85 degC, fIN 100 kHz), 70 dB min at 25 degC, no typical given for the A version; 28.9 mg step, 8.36 mg rms, 23 samples to reach 1.75 mg. I did not re-derive the 0.046 mg after 5 s, because it is not part of the refutation. 8.356 mg / sqrt(13,108 x 5) gives 0.033 mg, so the 0.046 mg assumes a per-channel rate the claim does not state. The scope is function: the error is in this function's reported figure, not in the part's lifecycle, maker or identity.
data.evidence: AD7476/AD7477/AD7478 Rev. F, Table 1, page 3, dynamic performance at fIN = 100 kHz. I read the page as rendered (pdftoppm, 110 dpi) and as pdftotext -layout. SINAD rows: A version 69 dB min and 70 dB min at TA = 25 degC. B version 70 dB min and 71.5 dB typ. S version 69 dB min and 70 dB min. The 71.5 sits under the B Version column header, and the A column is blank on the dB typ row. Footnote: temperature range for the A and B versions is -40 to +85 degC. Arithmetic (python3): ENOB = 11.1694 bits; step = (1/0.015 g) / 2^11.1694 = 28.945 mg; rms = 28.945 / 3.4641 = 8.3557 mg; ceil((8.3557 / 1.75)^2) = 23.
